section_summary.extract_value: This introduction discusses the increasing global prevalence of negative body image and eating disorders, moving beyond their traditional view as culture-bound syndromes. It highlights the role of modernization, urbanization, and globalization in promoting a thin ideal, and the impact of transmigration on body image, particularly for non-Western migrants. The present study (Study X) focuses on Zimbabwean women, comparing body image (operationalized as actual-ideal weight discrepancy and body appreciation) between those in Zimbabwe and those in Britain, hypothesizing more negative body image among the latter.
